ns2:group.ns2:title: Why Does Time Feel Faster As We Get Older?｜全英Talk：长大之后，时间越过越快？如何应对时间贫困？
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Do you ever feel like time moves faster as you get older?
In this video, I talk about why our perception of time changes as we age, why repetitive routines can make the years seem to disappear, and why new experiences often leave stronger memories.
But the deeper problem is something many of us struggle with: time poverty. Modern life gives us endless possibilities—books to read, skills to learn, places to visit, projects to pursue—but our time remains fundamentally limited.
Inspired in part by Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman, I reflect on a question that may be more important than becoming more productive:
How do we spend our limited time on the things that truly matter?
Perhaps the answer is not always to do more, but to make space, accept our limits, and choose more deliberately how we want to spend our lives.
What makes time feel slow—or fast—for you?

ns2:group.ns2:title: AI Won’t Make Everyone Smarter — It Will Widen the Cognitive Divide｜AI时代的残酷真相：会思考的人持续变强，不会思考的人沦为韭菜
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AI won’t make everyone smarter. If anything, it may widen the gap between those who can think critically and those who cannot. For people with strong judgment, AI can be an incredible tool for learning, creating, and boosting productivity. But for those who struggle to verify facts, question sources, or recognize misinformation, AI can also make them more vulnerable to hallucinations, manipulation, and even exploitation.
In this video, I talk about AI hallucinations, data poisoning, misinformation, and why critical thinking matters more than ever in the age of AI.
AI can give you answers—but it should never do your thinking for you. Stay curious. Stay skeptical. And always check the source.
AI不会让所有人同时变得更聪明，它更可能成为一个巨大的“认知放大器”：善于思考、懂得判断和核查信息的人，会借助AI变得越来越强；而缺乏批判性思维、习惯照单全收的人，则更容易被错误信息误导，甚至被操纵和收割。
在AI几乎可以随时给我们答案的时代，真正稀缺的能力或许不再是“知道答案”，而是判断：这个答案是真的吗？信息从哪里来？谁在提供它？背后有没有利益和偏见？
AI可以帮助我们思考，但不要把思考本身外包给AI。

你未必需要成为某个领域“最强的人”，但可以成为最会组合交叉优势、最能解决具体问题的人。

ns2:group.ns2:description:
In modern society, we have more freedom, more choices, and more possibilities than any generation before us.
But strangely, many young people feel more anxious, more confused, and more lost than ever.
Maybe the problem is not that you have no options. Maybe you simply have too many.
This video is about “liquid modernity,” freedom, uncertainty, social mobility, and why anxiety might actually be a sign of possibility.
As the philosopher Søren Kierkegaard once said: “Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.”
If you’re in your 20s and feel uncertain about life, career, identity, or the future — this video is for you.
You still have time. Your life is not a multiple-choice test. And there is more than one way to live a meaningful life.

ns2:group.ns2:title: 为什么现代人越来越不想结婚？《生育制度》讲透了整个逻辑
ns2:group.ns2:description:
结婚率走低、离婚率攀升，我们正站在传统与现代的十字路口。 婚姻，到底是为爱情，还是为合伙养娃？生育，是本能，还是一项“社会义务”？“父爱如山”，究竟是本能，还是被规训出的责任？
本期视频，我们深度拆解社会学经典《生育制度》。费孝通先生早在几十年前，就用四个扎心却深刻的观点，说透了一切。 01:28 生育是“损己利人”的文化设计，而非本能； 03:34 “父爱”是社会规训的产物； 06:35 传统婚姻的核心是确立抚育结构，而非爱情； 10:13 亲子矛盾，本质是社会规训与个体的冲突 15:05 清醒选择
看懂这套运行千年的“社会剧本”，不是为了否定婚姻与家庭，而是为了不被其绑架。我们将探讨： 🔹 在“重责任”的传统与“要爱情”的现代之间，如何抉择？ 🔹 面对催婚催育，如何区分“社会任务”与“自我意愿”？ 🔹 原生家庭的创伤，根源何在？我们又该如何“社会性断乳”？
希望这期视频，能给你提供一个清醒的框架。看清规则，不是要反对一切，而是为了在理解之后，做出真正忠于自己的选择。 无论结婚与否，生育与否，那都应该是你清醒的、自由的决定。
